From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). 7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Threshold point: the Seller's "settled" framing is not binding

The Seller's package says that clauses marked **[STANDARD]** are "reviewed and cleared by both sides," that the positions are "FINAL," and that the reviewer should "focus only on anything marked [OPEN]." Nothing in it is marked [OPEN]. The labels and the "market context" preamble are the Seller's own advocacy, so I have reviewed every item on its merits.

**Action:** Confirm with Wattlebridge principals whether anything was actually agreed at principal level. Unless a signed term sheet or email confirmation says otherwise, treat all items as open.

**Staleness:** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at **22 September 2026**, which is about six weeks before today. Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006 and Sandbar may all have moved. Require a current update, and do not let it operate as a disclosure against warranties repeated at Completion.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer should want:** A cap of at least 40–50% of price (AUD 9.6m–12m), or 20% only if backed by W&I cover with Seller retention. Fundamental, title, tax and specific indemnities should sit **outside** this cap.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 50%.** The risk is concentrated (30% customer dependency, a live privacy incident, an IP chain gap), so 20% is light for this target.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket (cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis. AUD 250k basket, with only the excess recoverable (deductible).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - De minimis of about AUD 10–15k, with related claims aggregated.
  - Basket of about AUD 120k (0.5%), structured as **tipping** (first dollar recoverable once exceeded).
  - Neither threshold to apply to fundamental, tax or specific-indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** A deductible basket at 1% permanently writes off AUD 250k of loss. Tipping is the buyer-protective norm.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months for general claims. Any limitation applies to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer should want:**
  - 24 months for general warranties, so the period covers at least one full audit cycle post-Completion.
  - Tax: until the ATO amendment period closes plus 6 months, or a minimum of 5–7 years.
  - Title and capacity: 7+ years or the statutory limitation period.
  - Specific indemnities: their own periods.
  - Delete the "applies to all Claims" default.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the catch-all and counter at 24 months.** The default silently imports 18 months into every claim category.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties are subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties capped at 100% of price, with a long time limit, no de minimis or basket, and no qualification by disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** If title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing. A 20% cap and 18-month window is not a simplification; it guts the core warranty.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature." There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out from all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance for fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct and wilful concealment by the Seller, its officers or the Company's management.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert the carve-out.** As drafted, the clause could cap or extinguish recovery for deliberate misstatement, and the non-reliance wording undermines misleading-conduct claims.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7 / DL 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room as at 22 September 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Only specific disclosures in the letter count, and only if fair (sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter).
  - No general data-room disclosure.
  - Public records limited to named searches (ASIC, PPSR) on a stated date.
  - No disclosure against fundamental warranties, the tax indemnity or specific indemnities.
  - The DL 1.4 non-admission wording must not dilute the fair-disclosure standard.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject general disclosure.** It shifts the entire data room's risk onto the Buyer and empties the warranties.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. This is actual plus constructive knowledge.
- **Buyer should want:** The opposite position (pro-sandbagging). The Buyer's knowledge, actual, constructive or imputed, does not reduce any claim, except for matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete and replace.** Combined with general disclosure, this clause would bar almost every claim, including those for issues this review has itself identified.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. The condition is "treated as satisfied" on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. DL 2 confirms that no consent has been obtained and the cl 11.3 conditions are not shown as satisfied.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A Condition Precedent requiring Bluefen's written, unconditional consent (or conditions acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably), in a form approved by the Buyer.
  - Evidence that all DD-002 cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
  - The consent not withdrawn or varied at Completion.
  - Seller best endeavours; the condition waivable only by the Buyer; a sunset date and walk right.
  - Consider a price adjustment, deferred consideration or specific indemnity if Bluefen terminates or reprices within 12 months.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (AUD 3.6m), and "consent delivered" does not equal "conditions satisfied."

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Seller:** Release of the approximately AUD 3.2m facility "to be provided following Completion." DL 3 says the facility is not repaid and has no discharge.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The outstanding amount paid out of the price at Completion, treated as Debt under the debt-free/cash-free mechanism.
  - A payoff letter before Completion.
  - At Completion: a signed deed of release, PPSR financing change statements or discharges, and the return of any title documents.
  - Confirmation that the change-of-control clause (cl 8.1) is not triggered pre-payout, or a waiver.
  - An indemnity for any shortfall.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** A post-Completion release leaves secured debt, and possibly security over the shares themselves, in a company the Buyer owns, which defeats debt-free pricing.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005)
- **Seller:** AUD 420k of Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow. DL 5 does not address on-costs.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Bonuses plus all on-costs (PAYG withholding, NSW payroll tax, superannuation if applicable, workers' compensation) treated as Transaction Expenses or Debt.
  - Those amounts deducted from the price, paid through Company payroll at Completion, and itemised in the funds flow.
  - A specific indemnity for any shortfall or later-triggered amounts.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** The Company, not the Seller, is the employer and payer. If the bonuses are not itemised, the Buyer funds about AUD 420k+ after paying full price.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate."
- **What DD-004 and DD-010 actually show:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. AUD 180k is recorded as open. There is no payment receipt and no assignment.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A Completion deliverable consisting of evidence that all SOW3 fees are paid, Ironquay's written confirmation, and an executed confirmatory IP assignment, with moral-rights consents where relevant.
  - Alternatively, a CP or escrow.
  - A specific indemnity covering all loss from any defect in title to the SOW3 materials, including third-party infringement claims, re-development or licensing costs, and customer claims.
  - That indemnity outside the cap, basket and disclosure, with at least a 6-year time limit.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as inadequate.** The real risk is that the Company does not own its product IP, not the AUD 180k invoice.

### SPA-N-012: Export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6, DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material."
- **What DL 6 actually shows:** A download link went to an unintended external address. About 1,240 records of personal information may be affected. Whether the file was accessed is unknown, and no notification assessment has been made.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - An immediate update covering the forensic findings, access logs, link expiry, and the outcome of the Privacy Act eligible data breach assessment. The 30-day assessment window has likely already passed, so ask whether the OAIC and affected individuals have been notified.
  - Pre-Completion conduct covenants on how the incident is handled.
  - A specific indemnity, outside the cap, basket, disclosure and knowledge qualifiers, covering notification and remediation costs, third-party and customer claims, and regulatory investigation costs, with penalties covered to the extent lawfully indemnifiable.
  - Consider escrow or a retention.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the materiality characterisation.** The incident is unresolved, possibly notifiable, and possibly already out of time, and the Seller is disclosing it to escape warranty liability.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Issue:** DL 8 says they should be read together, and it does not say whether they are committed, terminable or accrued. The split looks designed to stay under an approval or material-contract threshold.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Copies and dates of all three renewals.
  - Confirmation of who authorised them and whether they were committed after the locked-box or signing date.
  - Termination rights.
  - Any unpaid or uncommitted-but-unavoidable amounts treated as liabilities or Debt in the completion mechanics, or a specific indemnity.
  - Conduct-of-business covenants that aggregate related contracts, and related claims aggregated for thresholds.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "ordinary course" label.** AUD 330k of linked commitments needs proper scrutiny and price protection.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** All items pre-labelled [STANDARD]. A single limitation regime "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." Fundamental, tax and IP are collapsed into the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** Distinct regimes, each with its own cap, time limit, threshold and disclosure rules:
  1. General warranties.
  2. Fundamental warranties (title and capacity).
  3. Tax warranties and tax indemnity.
  4. Specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark, Bluefen if agreed).
  5. Fraud, which is uncapped.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the single regime and disregard the [STANDARD] labels.** Collapsing the categories is the mechanism that makes every other concession bite.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the share register at DD-012. DL 10 concedes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The Buyer's own checks: ASIC company extract reconciled to the register, PPSR search against the Seller and over the shares (Riverlark may hold share security), the constitution and any shareholders' agreement (pre-emption waivers), and confirmation of no options, convertibles or ESOP.
  - At Completion: executed share transfers, original certificates or a lost-certificate indemnity, releases of any share security, and director resignations and resolutions.
  - An uncapped title warranty.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not rely on DD-012 alone.** The Seller's own register is not independent proof of unencumbered title to 100%.

### SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller:** Considered "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity, outside the cap and disclosure, with an ATO-period time limit.
  - Tax warranties covering income tax, GST, payroll tax, PAYG, superannuation guarantee, contractor characterisation and any R&D tax incentive claims.
  - IP warranties covering ownership, contractor and employee assignments, open-source use and the Ironquay chain, with a higher cap and longer period.
- **Recommendation:** **Treat as OPEN and table the Buyer's drafts.** Nothing has been agreed, and SaaS tax and IP exposures do not fit an 18-month, 20% general regime.

---

## Priority summary
1. **Deal-breakers to fix before signing:** SPA-N-004, 005, 006, 007, 014. These limitation-architecture points neutralise everything else.
2. **Cash leakage at Completion:** SPA-N-009 (AUD 3.2m), 010 (AUD 420k+ plus on-costs), 013 (AUD 330k).
3. **Value and existential risk:** SPA-N-008 (Bluefen, 30% of revenue), 011 (product IP ownership), 012 (privacy incident), 015 (title).

These positions should be confirmed by NSW-qualified deal counsel before the mark-up issues, particularly on Privacy Act timing, payroll tax and superannuation treatment of the bonuses, and limitation periods.

- **What DL 6 actually shows:** A download link went to an unintended external address. About 1,240 records of personal information may be affected. Whether the file was accessed is unknown, and no notification assessment has been made.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - An immediate update covering the forensic findings, access logs, link expiry, and the outcome of the Privacy Act eligible data breach assessment. The 30-day assessment window has likely already passed, so ask whether the OAIC and affected individuals have been notified.
  - Pre-Completion conduct covenants on how the incident is handled.
  - A specific indemnity, outside the cap, basket, disclosure and knowledge qualifiers, covering notification and remediation costs, third-party and customer claims, and regulatory investigation costs, with penalties covered to the extent lawfully indemnifiable.
  - Consider escrow or a retention.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the materiality characterisation.** The incident is unresolved, possibly notifiable, and possibly already out of time, and the Seller is disclosing it to escape warranty liability.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Issue:** DL 8 says they should be read together, and it does not say whether they are committed, terminable or accrued. The split looks designed to stay under an approval or material-contract threshold.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Copies and dates of all three renewals.
  - Confirmation of who authorised them and whether they were committed after the locked-box or signing date.
  - Termination rights.
  - Any unpaid or uncommitted-but-unavoidable amounts treated as liabilities or Debt in the completion mechanics, or a specific indemnity.
  - Conduct-of-business covenants that aggregate related contracts, and related claims aggregated for thresholds.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "ordinary course" label.** AUD 330k of linked commitments needs proper scrutiny and price protection.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** All items pre-labelled [STANDARD]. A single limitation regime "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." Fundamental, tax and IP are collapsed into the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** Distinct regimes, each with its own cap, time limit, threshold and disclosure rules:
  1. General warranties.
  2. Fundamental warranties (title and capacity).
  3. Tax warranties and tax indemnity.
  4. Specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark, Bluefen if agreed).
  5. Fraud, which is uncapped.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the single regime and disregard the [STANDARD] labels.** Collapsing the categories is the mechanism that makes every other concession bite.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the share register at DD-012. DL 10 concedes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The Buyer's own checks: ASIC company extract reconciled to the register, PPSR search against the Seller and over the shares (Riverlark may hold share security), the constitution and any shareholders' agreement (pre-emption waivers), and confirmation of no options, convertibles or ESOP.
  - At Completion: executed share transfers, original certificates or a lost-certificate indemnity, releases of any share security, and director resignations and resolutions.
  - An uncapped title warranty.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not rely on DD-012 alone.** The Seller's own register is not independent proof of unencumbered title to 100%.

### SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller:** Considered "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity, outside the cap and disclosure, with an ATO-period time limit.
  - Tax warranties covering income tax, GST, payroll tax, PAYG, superannuation guarantee, contractor characterisation and any R&D tax incentive claims.
  - IP warranties covering ownership, contractor and employee assignments, open-source use and the Ironquay chain, with a higher cap and longer period.
- **Recommendation:** **Treat as OPEN and table the Buyer's drafts.** Nothing has been agreed, and SaaS tax and IP exposures do not fit an 18-month, 20% general regime.
